_meta.indication: Indicated as a component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen for the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in pediatric and young adult patients age 1 month to 21 years.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, open-label study comparing intravenous calaspargase pegol every 3 weeks to intravenous pegaspargase (Oncaspar) every 2 weeks on a DFCI ALL Consortium backbone; designed to determine whether an every-3-week regimen provided NSAA comparable to pegaspargase every 2 weeks with comparable safety and no erosion in EFS/OS (not powered for clinical superiority/non-inferiority).
pivotal_trials.population: Children and adolescents with newly diagnosed acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and lymphoblastic lymphoma (LL) treated with the DFCI ALL Consortium therapeutic backbone.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was pharmacokinetic: maintenance of nadir serum asparaginase activity (NSAA) at or above the therapeutic threshold of 0.1 U/mL (clinical efficacy endpoints such as CR/MRD/EFS/OS were not primary).
pivotal_trials.n: DFCI 11-001 randomized n=239 (calaspargase n=119, pegaspargase n=120); efficacy determination drew on 124 patients from supportive Study AALL07P4.
pivotal_trials.result: 123 (99%, 95% CI: 96% - 100%) of the 124 patients maintained NSAA > 0.1 U/mL at weeks 6, 12, 18, 24 and 30; population PK imputation showed more than 99% of subjects maintained steady-state NSAA above 0.1 U/mL up to 30 weeks.

key_safety: Most common grade >=3 adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) were elevated transaminase (52% vs 66% pegaspargase), bilirubin increased (20% vs 25%), pancreatitis (18% vs 24%), and abnormal clotting studies (14% vs 21%). Serious risks include hypersensitivity (grade 3-4 including anaphylaxis, 7 to 21%), pancreatitis (12 to 16%), thrombosis, hemorrhage, and hepatotoxicity.
target_moa: An asparagine-specific enzyme; L-asparaginase catalyzes conversion of L-asparagine into aspartic acid and ammonia, and the therapeutic effect is thought to result from selective killing of leukemic cells that depend on an exogenous source of L-asparagine due to depletion of plasma L-asparagine.
modality: Enzyme (pegylated form of E. coli-derived L-asparaginase with a succinimidyl carbamate linker).

rems.type: FDA review determined that a REMS is not necessary; labeling including Warnings and Precautions will be used to communicate safety issues.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed by an advisory committee.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Designation originally granted for pegaspargase for treatment of acute lymphocytic leukemia (10/20/1989); Office of Orphan Products Development confirmed the designation was applicable to calaspargase pegol-mknl.

citations.quote: On 10/20/1989, the Applicant was granted Orphan Designation for pegaspargase for treatment of acute lymphocytic leukemia. The Office of Orphan Products Development confirmed that the designation was applicable to calaspargase pegol-mknl.

summary.text: ASPARLAS was submitted as an original 351(a) BLA with standard (non-priority) review and approved as a regular (full) approval, not under accelerated approval. Efficacy was established on the basis of achievement and maintenance of nadir serum asparaginase activity (NSAA) above 0.1 U/mL. Orphan designation (originally for pegaspargase in acute lymphocytic leukemia) was confirmed applicable to calaspargase pegol-mknl, and the drug was designated for a rare pediatric disease.

citations.quote:
Application Type	Original 351(a)
Priority or Standard	Standard

The review team recommends regular approval of calaspargase pegol-mknl for the indication “as a component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen for the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in pediatric and young adult patients age 1 month to 21 years” using a dose of 2,500 units/m2 given intravenously no more frequently than every 21 days.

The determination of efficacy was based on a demonstration of the achievement and maintenance of nadir serum asparaginase activity (NSAA) above the level of 0.1 U/mL using calaspargase pegol-mknl 2500 U/m2 intravenously every 3 weeks.
On 10/25/2017, calaspargase pegol for treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) was designated as a drug for a rare pediatric disease.
